guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not treating Purdue’s opening win as proof, but the shape of that performance supports why our numbers are more favorable to the home team than the market. Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns, while Purdue’s defense held Indiana State to 284 total yards and 66 on the ground. The defense also generated eight tackles for loss and three sacks, giving us some evidence that Purdue can disrupt drives rather than needing its offense to win a shootout.

The meaningful concern for us is Wake Forest’s explosiveness. Gio Lopez threw for 350 yards and three touchdowns without an interception in his debut, and Wake Forest did not allow a sack. Purdue also had 38 players make their team debuts in its opener, so Wake Forest’s ability to create chunk plays is a real test for a heavily reworked roster. Still, our view is that the market is placing too much separation between these teams. We do not need Purdue to reproduce its opening offensive output; we need the home team to remain competitive, and its defensive performance and experienced quarterback give us a credible path.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Purdue’s offense against Wake Forest’s defense. Our efficiency numbers rate this as the clearest obstacle for Purdue, particularly through the air, and Purdue had six offensive linemen make their first starts for the program in the opener. Wake Forest’s defense recorded seven tackles for loss and two sacks against Akron, so Browne may not get the same clean operating environment he had in Week 1.

What matters for our position is whether Purdue can finish the opportunities it creates. Purdue converted 6 of 11 third downs and scored on all six red-zone trips in the opener. We are not assuming that efficiency carries over unchanged, but enough drive sustainability would keep Wake Forest from creating the margin the market is asking it to produce.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest opened the 2026 season with a 38-16 home win over Akron on Sept. 3.
Wake Forest produced 559 total yards against Akron, including 356 passing yards and 203 rushing yards.
Wake Forest did not commit a turnover against Akron and recovered one Akron fumble.
Wake Forest converted 7 of 15 third downs and both of its fourth-down attempts against Akron.
Wake Forest's defense allowed Akron 305 total yards, including 149 rushing and 156 passing, while recording seven tackles for loss and two sacks.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue opened its season with a 44-19 win over Indiana State on Sept. 4.
Purdue gained 523 total yards against Indiana State, including 346 passing yards and 177 rushing yards.
Purdue scored on all six of its red-zone opportunities and converted 6 of 11 third downs against Indiana State.
Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions against Indiana State.

Eleven Purdue players caught a pass in the opener; Asaad Waseem led the team with 107 receiving yards and a touchdown on six catches, while Xavier Townsend had a team-high seven receptions for 47 yards.
Purdue running back Fame Ijeboi rushed 11 times for 87 yards and a touchdown, averaging 7.9 yards per attempt against Indiana State.
Purdue held Indiana State to 284 total yards and 66 rushing yards while recording eight tackles for loss and three sacks.
Purdue defensive back Mister Clark recorded five solo tackles, two tackles for loss and one sack in the opener.
Purdue senior Don Saunders recorded the Boilermakers' only takeaway against Indiana State with the sixth interception of his career.

quarterback.fact: Gio Lopez is Wake Forest's projected starting quarterback and a 2026 team captain after transferring from North Carolina.
In his Wake Forest debut, Lopez completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed seven times for 39 yards.
Lopez's 78-yard touchdown pass to Carlos Hernandez against Akron was the longest completion of his collegiate career.
Lopez previously played at South Alabama under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell.
Through 28 career games and 24 starts, Lopez has completed 65.8 percent of his passes for 5,131 yards, 35 touchdowns and 12 interceptions and has rushed for 791 yards and 12 touchdowns.
